author: Thomas
case: In re Trans World Airlines, Inc.
form: One signed opinion following full merits submission resolves the transferred-property interest, independent monetary-satisfaction predicate, claimant-process scope and resulting sale and ancillary-appeal dispositions. The propositions share one complete nine-Justice ground; neither division nor combination responds to counts.
fit: Fit governs. Thomas's Hartford Underwriters and Noland work addresses the Code's particular grants of authority and rejects outcome-driven substitution for enacted requirements. His frozen position carries both the breadth of interest and the separate legal capacity for monetary satisfaction, which is the opinion's central distinction. Souter is a strong alternative through his Dow Corning opinion, but Thomas has the lower count and can explain the specific source equally faithfully. Stone-Zsela fully joins the shared ground; his approved formulation supplies no unique accommodation or coordination advantage requiring self-assignment. No expansion or reassignment is necessary. The full opinion retains every Associate's recorded scope condition.
